editions.headline: Hormuz Deal “On the Verge of Being Finalised,” Iran Says — But Tolls Remain the Sticking Point
editions.teaser: Iran says its Hormuz agreement with Oman is "on the verge of being finalised," with shipping coordinates agreed after three-plus weeks of talks, but a genuine sticking point remains: the U.S. wants toll-free passage while Iran signals it will introduce a fee system for vessels, and Iran insists the U.S. must meet its own commitments before the strait fully reopens; Trump says "a lot of progress has been made"; Wall Street takes a breather after its huge rally, with the Dow notching yet another record close (54,349, +263 points) while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq dip slightly on profit-taking; gold surges toward $4,300 for a fourth straight gain, up nearly 6% on the week, even as oil extends its slide to $74.79 and rate-hike odds ease; Bitcoin firms to around $64,650 for a third straight day, nearing its $65,300 resistance; Armstrong Economics turns to Europe, forecasting eurozone stagflation bottoming around 2028; Chicago sees showers and clouds near 76°F, and the Cubs (65-49) complete a sweep of the Dodgers behind a two-homer game from Crow-Armstrong while the White Sox (59-53, still atop the AL Central) are swept by a red-hot Red Sox team.

editions.headline: “The Deal Is Now Complete”: U.S. and Iran Reach Framework Agreement to End the War
editions.teaser: The U.S. and Iran announce a framework deal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with Trump declaring "the deal with the Islamic Republic of Iran is now complete"; the reported 14-point memorandum covers a broader end to hostilities including in Lebanon and a U.S. troop withdrawal, while a 60-day Oman-Iran arrangement governs safe passage through Hormuz and CENTCOM confirms the strait's southern route is "free and open"; the reversal caps a week that began with Iran firing missiles at U.S. forces just seven days earlier; markets, already rallying hard, closed Tuesday with the Dow above 54,000 for the first time (+907 points), the S&P 500 at a record 7,736.52, and the Nasdaq up 2.59%, while oil steadies near $76 after Tuesday's 5% plunge; June JOLTS shows job openings little changed at 7.4 million; Bitcoin holds steady near $64,150; Armstrong Economics cautions that even a real peace deal doesn't retire its 2026 Directional Change thesis; Chicago sees cloudy skies with afternoon storms, and the Cubs (64-49) beat the Dodgers while the White Sox (59-52, still atop the AL Central) are routed by a red-hot Red Sox team.

editions.headline: Hormuz Deal Could Land “Today or Tomorrow” as Wall Street Rides a Record Rally Into August
editions.teaser: Treasury Secretary Bessent says a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come "today or tomorrow" as Qatar describes broader U.S.-Iran talks as "in very progressive stages" with draft agreements circulating, even as Trump called Iranian leadership "unbelievably duplicitous" over the weekend after Tehran's latest denial; Iran separately negotiates a temporary Oman-brokered safe shipping route through the strait; Wall Street rides a record rally into August, with the Dow closing at a record high Monday (+~700 points) and continuing higher Tuesday as Caterpillar surges 12% on record sales and Palantir soars 18% on an "otherworldly" quarter; oil extends its plunge, falling another 4.6% to $76.66 on Hormuz optimism; Bitcoin recovers to around $63,776 as crypto watches the CLARITY Act's August 10 deadline, with 2026 passage odds slipping; Armstrong Economics says diplomatic progress and denial can coexist within its 2026 Directional Change thesis; Chicago enjoys a sunny, pleasant Tuesday near 79°F, the IRS Nationwide Tax Forum opens in New Orleans, and the Cubs (63-49) rout the Dodgers 10-5 while the White Sox (59-51, still atop the AL Central) open a series at Boston after Monday's off day.

editions.headline: Trump Calls Off “Massive” Strike on Iran, Announces New Talks Monday — Oil Plunges, Wall Street Rallies to Start August
editions.teaser: Trump calls off what he says would have been "the biggest attack since World War II" on Iran, crediting pressure from allies including Saudi Arabia, and announces new talks with Iran set to begin Monday covering the Strait of Hormuz and denuclearization; Iran's Foreign Ministry flatly denies any negotiations are planned, extending the war's recurring pattern of claim and denial; Wall Street rallies to start August (S&P 500 +0.64%, Dow +1.2%, Nasdaq +0.49%) as oil plunges 4.7% to $80.72 on the deflating attack risk premium and gold climbs back above $4,050; CME FedWatch shows a sharp hawkish shift with 64.5% odds of a September rate hike; Bitcoin pulls back to around $62,650 despite the de-escalation, decoupled as it has been for weeks; Armstrong Economics reads the sharp reversal as confirmation of its 2026 Directional Change thesis; Chicago enjoys a warm, sunny Monday near 82°F, and the MLB trade deadline brings the Cubs a rotation overhaul (Kevin Gausman in, Jameson Taillon out) while the White Sox (59-51, still atop the AL Central) add bullpen depth.

editions.headline: Trump Weighs Iran Energy Strikes Discussed at Camp David as Tehran Warns of “Full-Scale Regional War”
editions.teaser: The plan to strike Iran's energy infrastructure, first reported Saturday, was discussed at Trump's Camp David cabinet meeting Friday, with Israel notified and coordinating on the potential operation though no final order has been given; Iran's Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi warns the U.S. is "moving at an accelerating pace to fan the flames of a full-scale regional war" as the Pentagon declines to discuss targets before Trump decides; markets, closed Sunday, head into a pivotal week with earnings season running hot (85% of S&P 500 reporters beating estimates, profits tracking +47%) and a packed calendar including McDonald's, Costco, Disney, Palantir, and AMD; oil opens flat at $83.92, suggesting traders are still waiting on confirmation rather than pricing in the worst case, while Bitcoin recovers to around $63,455 from Saturday's two-week low; Armstrong Economics says a war aimed at energy infrastructure fits its 2026 Directional Change thesis of expanding rather than resolving conflict; Chicago sees a cloudy, breezy Sunday with morning showers clearing, and the Cubs (62-48) beat the Yankees while the White Sox (58-51) are shut out by the Rays but remain atop the AL Central ahead of Monday's MLB trade deadline.

editions.headline: U.S. and Israel Prepare a Weekend Bombardment of Iran's Energy Infrastructure as Trump Weighs the Final Order
editions.teaser: The U.S. and Israel prepare what could be one of the harshest bombing campaigns yet against Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possible over the weekend though Trump has not given a final order, as officials reportedly hope to conclude before markets open Monday; a tanker is struck by an unknown projectile near the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump downplays reports Iran was behind a Minnesota infrastructure cyberattack; Wall Street closes out a wild July with its first winning week in three (S&P 500 +0.7%, Dow +0.5%, Nasdaq +1% Friday) as Amazon surges nearly 15% on its biggest single-day gain in over a decade while Apple tumbles 7.2% on weak Services and China revenue; gold settles July near $4,076, WTI holds near $84.61, and Bitcoin drifts to a two-week low around $62,950 ahead of a tense weekend; Armstrong Economics's Socrates system gives "zero chance" a ceasefire holds as the war expands globally; Chicago sees a soggy Lollapalooza Saturday with storms lingering into the afternoon, and the Cubs (61-48) and White Sox (58-50, still atop the AL Central) both make moves ahead of Monday's MLB trade deadline.

editions.headline: Iranian Cleric Calls a Cease-Fire “a Deception” as the U.S. and Israel Weigh a Land Blockade — Wall Street Rallies on Cooler Inflation Before Apple and Amazon Split Investors
editions.teaser: A senior Iranian cleric tells Friday prayer-goers that any cease-fire would be "a deception" meant to let Washington redeploy forces, as the Telegraph reports the U.S. and Israel are discussing a land blockade of Iran to tighten economic pressure; Wall Street rallies hard Thursday (Dow +1.2% to 52,208.06, S&P 500 +1.7% to 7,437.64, Nasdaq +2.8% to 25,122.18) on a cooler Core PCE inflation reading (3.3% YoY in June) that undercuts fears the Fed's Wednesday hold left it behind the curve; Big Tech earnings split investors Friday as Amazon crushes estimates (shares +12% premarket) while Apple beats but guides soft on supply constraints (shares -7% premarket); Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage jumps to a one-year high of 6.66%, gold holds near $4,086 on dollar weakness, and Bitcoin drifts to around $63,875; Armstrong Economics calls a potential land blockade the next rung on the same escalation ladder; Chicago braces for weekend storms that could disrupt Lollapalooza, with the Cubs taking their series in St. Louis (61-47) and the White Sox sweeping past the Yankees in extra innings (57-50).

editions.headline: U.S. Completes a “Heavy Wave” of Retaliatory Strikes on Iran as Tehran Vows to “Punish the Aggressor Today”
editions.teaser: The U.S. completes a "heavy wave" of retaliatory strikes on Iran overnight, delivering Trump's promised response to Tuesday's Iranian missile attack on U.S. forces in Jordan, as Iranian state media report three civilians killed and Iran's Revolutionary Guard says three of its own personnel died; Iran vows to "punish the aggressor today" and warns Saudi Arabia and Jordan they will face a "harsh response" for aiding the U.S., as the war widens with active fronts now including the Houthis, Hezbollah, and Saudi Arabia; markets are still absorbing Wednesday's brutal selloff (Dow -2.19% to 51,594.14, S&P 500 -1.52% to 7,316.15, Nasdaq -1.74% to 24,442.94) after bond yields spiked on fears the Fed's hold leaves it behind on inflation, even as Thursday futures rebound (Dow +0.51%, S&P +0.4%, Nasdaq +1.86%) ahead of Core PCE data and Apple/Amazon earnings following Meta's strong beat; Brent crude surges past $90 on the retaliation, gold climbs toward $4,081, and Bitcoin holds near $64,490, still decoupled from the war and Fed headlines; Armstrong Economics says a war that widens rather than resolves fits its 2026 Directional Change thesis; Chicago warms back up to a sunny 83°F, with the Cubs falling to the Cardinals 3-2 in 10 innings (60-47) and the White Sox outlasting the Yankees 6-5 in 12 (56-50).

editions.headline: Iran Fires Missiles at U.S. Forces, Shattering the Pause, as the Fed Holds Rates Steady for a Fifth Straight Meeting
editions.teaser: Iran shatters a four-day pause with a surprise ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces, Jordan intercepting five inbound missiles as U.S. and Saudi forces retaliate with strikes on Iran-backed militia sites in eastern Iraq that kill more than 20 fighters; Trump vows the U.S. will hit back hard, telling Fox News "they're going to get a beating"; the Fed holds its benchmark rate at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting in Kevin Warsh's first decision as chair, offering little forward guidance amid reported dissents; Wall Street closes lower (Dow ~-0.7% to ~52,242, S&P 500 ~-0.2% to ~7,374, Nasdaq ~-0.2% to ~24,544) as oil spikes to $82.42 on the attack before reversing to ~$79.40; gold climbs to $4,043 and Bitcoin keeps grinding higher to ~$64,350, decoupled from the day's war and Fed headlines; Armstrong Economics says its warning that a pause is not a peace has been borne out; Chicago enjoys a second mild, comfortable day near 78°F, with the Cubs routing the Cardinals 10-2 to improve to 60-46 and the White Sox falling to the Yankees 3-2 to slip to 55-50.

editions.headline: Netanyahu and Trump Meet for the First Time Since the Iran War Began as a $250 Billion Nvidia-OpenAI Deal Triggers a Global Chip Rout
editions.teaser: Netanyahu meets Trump at the White House for the first time since the Iran war began, with Iran's Foreign Ministry flatly denying any talks are underway and Tehran vowing it "will never allow the United States to determine the timing of war and peace," even as the military pause holds into a fourth day; markets are rattled by a reported $250 billion Nvidia backstop for OpenAI's data-center financing, sending Nvidia down 5%, letting Apple reclaim the title of world's most valuable company at ~$4.95T, and dragging South Korea's Kospi down 10.8% as Samsung and SK Hynix plunge; U.S. stocks close mixed, with the Dow up 0.77% to 52,609.61, the S&P 500 off 0.33% to 7,388.38, and the Nasdaq down 1.36% to 24,593.43 as the Fed's two-day meeting opens ahead of Wednesday's decision; gold slips toward $4,030, oil steadies near $84 after Monday's plunge, and Bitcoin drifts to around $63,200; Armstrong Economics ties the AI financing jitters into its 2026 Directional Change thesis; Chicago enjoys a cooler, drier Tuesday in the mid-70s after Monday's storms, with the Cubs opening at St. Louis at 59-46 and the White Sox hosting the Yankees (Cole vs. Kay) at 55-49.

editions.headline: Iran and the U.S. Hold Fire for a Third Day as Trump Says “Good Things Can Happen” — Wall Street Steadies Into a Week of Fed and Big Tech Earnings
editions.teaser: The pause between the U.S. and Iran holds for a third straight day as Trump tells reporters he's in talks with Tehran and "good things can happen," though Iran's Foreign Ministry denies requesting formal negotiations and says mediators are only passing messages; Wall Street steadies into a week headlined by Wednesday's Fed decision and earnings from Microsoft, Meta, Apple, and Amazon, with the Dow up 0.51% to 52,210.08, the S&P 500 flat at 7,413.18, and the Nasdaq off 0.18% to 24,932.08 as chip stocks slide and SanDisk plunges 11%; gold climbs 1% toward $4,100 as oil eases further and Fed hike odds for July 29 cool to roughly 35% from last week's 38%; Bitcoin whipsaws from a $65,333 open down to around $63,754 by evening; Armstrong Economics warns a pause is not a peace as 2026's Directional Change keeps unfolding in smaller increments; a line of tornado-warned storms rakes Chicagoland with 5-inch hail near Lemont and gusts to 100 mph, knocking out power to 200,000+ ComEd customers, before a cold front clears the air for a cooler week; the Cubs sit idle at 59-46 ahead of a Milwaukee series while the White Sox fall 12-2 to the Yankees.

editions.headline: Washington Goes Quiet on Iran for a Second Straight Night as Oman Brokers Progress on Reopening the Strait of Hormuz
editions.teaser: For the first time since the campaign began July 6, the U.S. military reports no new strikes on Iran for a second consecutive night, as Iran's army says it has likewise halted retaliatory attacks and two regional sources tell CBS News that Oman-Iran talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz are making real progress; Vice President JD Vance and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine raise escalation concerns in a White House meeting as officials warn Patriot interceptor stockpiles can't sustain the current strike tempo; Ukraine's Zelenskyy accuses Russia of feeding Iran satellite imagery to target U.S. Gulf bases; Armstrong Economics ties JD Vance's break from Israel-centric foreign policy to his 2028 positioning; markets are closed Sunday after Friday's mixed close (S&P 500 +0.05% to 7,411.98, Dow +0.46% to 51,947.25, Nasdaq −0.64% to 24,975.82); Bitcoin ticks up to around $64,510; Fed rate-hike odds for Wednesday's meeting hold near 38%; the Cubs rout the Pirates 11-0 behind a Pete Crow-Armstrong near-cycle to improve to 59-45, while the White Sox fall to the Astros 4-1 but remain atop the AL Central at 54-49; Chicago bakes under a heat index near 100-105° with a severe storm risk arriving Monday morning.

editions.headline: Drones Strike Northern Iraq and Sirens Sound in Bahrain After a 13th Night of U.S. Strikes on Iran — Wall Street Closes a Volatile Week Little Changed as Oil Pulls Back From $100
editions.teaser: Explosive-laden drones target Irbil in northern Iraq and sirens sound in Bahrain and Jordan Friday after U.S. Central Command completes a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with fresh strikes reported on a Revolutionary Guard naval base, Qeshm Island, and sites in Isfahan and Khuzestan provinces; President Trump says he is weighing further escalation after Tehran rejected an Iraqi-brokered ceasefire proposal, even as he separately says Iran is “getting more serious” about talks; Wall Street closes a volatile week little changed, with the S&P 500 up 0.05% to 7,411.98, the Dow gaining 0.46% to 51,947.25, and the Nasdaq slipping 0.64% to 24,975.82 as a 3.5% jump in Apple offsets continued chip-sector weakness; Brent crude pulls back below $96 and WTI falls to $90.12 after briefly topping $100 Thursday, even as all three indexes finish the week lower; Fed rate-hike odds for the July 29 meeting hold near 38%, up from just 10.7% a week ago, as Chair Kevin Warsh's first live-hike test approaches; Bitcoin slips to around $64,029; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage holds at a one-year-high 6.58%; the Cubs rally past the Pirates 3-2 in 10 innings on a Dansby Swanson go-ahead single to improve to 58-45, while the White Sox fall to the Astros 9-5 but remain alone atop the AL Central at 54-48; Chicago enjoys a mild, partly sunny Saturday near 83°F before the weekend heat builds toward the low 90s.

editions.headline: Trump Threatens a “Massive Attack, Bigger Than Ever Before” as Iran Rejects a Ceasefire Offer and Oil Tops $100 — Tesla and Alphabet Selloff Sends Wall Street to Its Worst Day in a Month
editions.teaser: President Trump tells Axios he is weighing a “massive attack” on Iran, “bigger than ever before,” after Tehran rejects an Iraqi-mediated ceasefire proposal and U.S. strikes hit Iran for a 13th consecutive night; Iran retaliates on U.S.-linked targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, while Yemen's Houthi rebels claim fresh Red Sea attacks on Saudi shipping and Reuters reports Iran flew IRGC commanders into Yemen this month; Brent crude briefly topped $100 a barrel Thursday for the first time since May before easing toward $97; Wall Street closed Thursday at S&P 500 7,408.30 (−1.21%), Nasdaq 25,137.69 (−2.15%), Dow 51,711.65 (−0.97%), its worst session in a month, as Tesla cratered 14.5% on an earnings miss and negative free cash flow and Alphabet fell 7% despite beating on revenue after raising 2026 capex guidance to $205 billion; Fed hike odds for July 29 climbed toward 40% as the oil shock revives inflation fears; Bitcoin holds near $65,030 as gold pulls back to around $4,049; the White Sox host the Astros tonight alone atop the AL Central at 54-47, and the Cubs open a series at Pittsburgh at 57-45; Chicago enjoys a mostly sunny, pleasant Friday near 84°F.

editions.headline: Trump Vows to Bomb an Iranian Bridge or Power Plant for Every Ship Iran Hits in Hormuz as Houthis Strike Saudi Tankers and the War's Price Tag Hits $37.5 Billion
editions.teaser: President Trump warns the U.S. will destroy one Iranian bridge or power plant, including in Tehran, for every future attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz, as U.S. Central Command completes a 12th consecutive night of strikes and Yemen's Houthi rebels claim attacks on two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, opening a second maritime front; Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth tells the Senate the war has cost $37.5 billion so far and seeks $67 billion more; Brent crude tops $98 and WTI climbs above $90, six-week highs, as Alphabet beats on earnings but raises 2026 capex to $205 billion (shares down premarket) and Tesla posts its first negative free-cash-flow quarter in two years; Wall Street closed Wednesday at S&P 500 7,498.96 (-0.14%), Nasdaq 25,690.90 (-0.57%), Dow 52,218.58 (-0.01%); Fed hike odds for July 29 climb to roughly 36% as the oil shock complicates Chair Warsh's path; Bitcoin holds near $65,659 as gold gains 1.5% to $4,137; the White Sox beat the Rangers 4-2 to move alone atop the AL Central (54-47) while the Cubs fall to the Tigers 5-1 in their series finale (57-45); Chicago enjoys a mostly sunny, pleasant Thursday near 78°F with low humidity.

editions.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for an 11th Straight Night as the Campaign Widens to Tehran's Outskirts — Houthis Open a New Front With a Saudi Blockade
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command completes its 11th consecutive night of strikes on Iran, for the first time reaching the outskirts of Tehran and a military site near Tabriz in a departure from the campaign's earlier focus on southern Iran; Iran retaliates on U.S.-linked sites in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain, while Houthi rebels in Yemen declare a new naval blockade of Saudi Arabia, threatening the kingdom's Red Sea pipeline workaround; Pakistan hosts Iran's interior minister for revived diplomacy as Secretary of State Rubio says Tehran isn't "serious about talks"; oil jumps to 5-6 week highs (WTI ~$87, Brent ~$94) on the escalation; Wall Street closed Tuesday at S&P 500 7,509.20 (+0.89%), Nasdaq 25,837.21 (+1.29%), Dow ~52,223 (+0.74%) as chips rebounded, with Wednesday futures easing ahead of Alphabet and Tesla earnings after the close; CME FedWatch shows ~24% odds of a July 29 hike and ~69% odds of at least one hike by September as Cleveland Fed's Hammack joins the hawks; Bitcoin holds near $65,900; 30-year mortgage steady at 6.57% as existing home sales unexpectedly fell 2.4% in June; the Cubs rout the Tigers 11-2 to even their series (57-44) while the White Sox are blanked 10-0 by the Rangers with catcher Kyle Teel headed to the IL (53-47); Chicago sees a cooler, clearer Wednesday near 76°F as air quality improves, with a Beach Hazard Statement in effect for Lake Michigan.

editions.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran for a 10th Consecutive Night as Wall Street Looks Past the War Toward a Marquee Earnings Week
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command carries out a tenth straight night of strikes on Iran, hitting military command centers, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defense systems, with explosions reported in Bandar Abbas, Qeshm, Shiraz, Isfahan, Bandar Lengeh, Chabahar, and Konarak; the IRGC claims retaliatory strikes on U.S.-linked targets in Kuwait and Bahrain and says two more tankers were disabled in the Strait of Hormuz, while Jordan intercepts five Iranian drones; Trump warns on Truth Social that Iran "will pay for that killing many times over," and the U.S. death toll holds at 18 after a brutal weekend, with a Dover AFB dignified transfer postponed; Wall Street mostly looks past the war as chip stocks rebound (Nasdaq 100 futures +1.3%, KOSPI +3.6%) and 3M and GM both beat earnings estimates ahead of Alphabet, Tesla, Intel and IBM reporting later this week; oil eases from Monday's spike (WTI ~$82.56, Brent ~$88-90) on reports Iran is weighing mediator proposals; Bitcoin climbs back above $66,000 as Cleveland Fed's Hammack joins hawkish voices pushing December hike odds to 80%; the White Sox rout the Rangers 10-3 to snap a 10-game Globe Life skid (53-46) while the Cubs fall to the Tigers 8-6 in 10 innings (56-44); Chicago sees hazy skies near 84°F with air quality improving toward moderate and another late-day storm chance before a cooler midweek.

editions.headline: U.S. Death Toll Hits 18 as Ninth Night of Strikes Pounds Iran — Wall Street Shrugs It Off Again as Chips Rebound and Oil Pares a 4% Spike
editions.teaser: The Pentagon confirms a third U.S. service member died over the weekend disposing of a downed Iranian drone in northern Iraq, pushing the American death toll to 18 and closing out the war's worst 72-hour stretch for U.S. forces after Friday's fatal strike on Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base; CENTCOM recovers the remains of the previously missing soldier as the U.S. launches a ninth straight night of strikes and surges additional F-16s and F-35s into the region even as officials warn munitions stockpiles are thinning; Iran retaliates by striking Jordan's Aqaba airport, U.S.-linked bases in Kuwait, and targets in Syria, while the IRGC claims two tankers were “forced to cease movement” in the Strait of Hormuz and Kuwait's desalination plant is hit for a second straight day; Trump says Iran has been “very, very badly damaged,” while Rubio says the U.S. remains open to diplomacy as Iran signals it will weigh mediator proposals, pulling Brent back from an overnight spike to $90.79 and WTI back from $84.68; Wall Street mostly shrugs it off, with the S&P 500 up 0.63%, Nasdaq up 1.02%, and Dow up 0.23% at midday as chips rebound into a heavy earnings week; gas prices top a national $4/gallon average; Andy Burnham is sworn in as UK prime minister; Armstrong Economics warns “wars end with an invoice” as the IMF cuts global growth to ~3%, and reports Iran has warned UAE airports to prepare for evacuation; the Cubs (56-43) rout the Twins 10-1 behind Imanaga's seven shutout innings and the White Sox (52-46) blank the Blue Jays 3-0 to take the series, with both clubs opening new series today; Chicago sees hazy skies near 84°F with an air quality alert through tonight and a slight risk of severe storms this evening, damaging winds the top concern.

editions.headline: Iran Declares the MOU “Suspended” After an Eighth Night of U.S. Strikes as the American Death Toll Climbs to 16
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command carries out an eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran early Sunday, hitting an under-construction nuclear power plant near Bandar Abbas and Qeshm Island, as Tehran declares the 60-day memorandum of understanding “suspended” following Friday's deadliest attack yet: two U.S. service members killed and a third missing after Iran struck Jordan's Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, bringing the American death toll in the war to 16; Kuwait's power and desalination plant is hit for a second straight day, and Bahrain and Kuwait both report intercepting fresh Iranian aerial attacks Sunday morning; Wall Street closed Friday on its worst week in months (S&P 500 -1.01% to 7,457.69, Nasdaq -1.40% to 25,520.24, Dow -406.55 to 52,146.42; week: S&P -1.6%, Nasdaq -2.9%) as the PHLX Semiconductor Index confirmed a bear market; oil surged into the weekend, with Brent settling at $88.10 (+4.6%, +16% on the week) and WTI at $82.49 (+4.5%); Bitcoin holds near $64,850, up from Friday's $62,810 low; gold ticks back above $4,000 to ~$4,017; Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage holds at 6.55%, a third straight weekly increase, as NAR reports June's median existing home price hit a record $440,600; the White Sox (51-46) stay alone in first place in the AL Central after a 1-0 loss to Toronto Saturday, and the Cubs (55-43) bounce back 6-2 over the Twins, with both clubs playing series finales today; Chicago sees hazy sunshine and mid-80s with an Air Quality Alert extended through Monday for wildfire smoke, ahead of a severe storm threat Monday.

editions.headline: Iran War Fallout Deepens Into the Weekend as 10,000 Lose Water and Bahrain Intercepts Fresh Strikes — Wall Street Closes Its Worst Week in Months
editions.teaser: Iran's national water company says roughly 10,000 people across 20 villages are without water after Friday night's seventh consecutive round of U.S. strikes; Wall Street closes its worst week in months as the PHLX Semiconductor Index confirms a bear market; Bitcoin recovers to ~$64,100; the White Sox rout the Blue Jays 12-4, the Cubs fall to the Twins 5-2; Chicago sees a warm, hazy Saturday near 87°.

editions.headline: Seventh Day of Strikes Hits Iranian Bridges and Rail as Tehran Strikes Al Udeid and Kuwait — Chip Selloff Deepens as Netflix Slides on Weak Q3 Guide
editions.teaser: U.S. strikes hit bridges, a railway junction, and an airport across Hormozgan and Sistan-Baluchestan provinces overnight; Iran retaliates striking Qatar's Al Udeid Air Base and Kuwait/Bahrain infrastructure; oil climbs on the escalation; Bitcoin slips to about $62,800; the Cubs host the Twins and White Sox open at Toronto.

editions.headline: Sixth Night of Strikes Brings Sirens to Bahrain and Kuwait as Trump Weighs Seizing Iran's Main Oil Terminal — UnitedHealth's Blowout Offsets a Chip Wobble
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command strikes Iran for a sixth straight day and disables a tanker headed for Kharg Island; UnitedHealth jumps 7% on an earnings beat; Bitcoin holds near $64,750; Fed Chair Warsh wraps two days of congressional testimony.

editions.headline: Fifth Night of Strikes Collides With Warsh's Senate Showdown — Cooling PPI and a $65K Bitcoin Breakout Lift Wall Street
editions.teaser: U.S. Central Command strikes Iran for a fifth straight day; Warsh's Senate testimony turns adversarial with Elizabeth Warren; June PPI falls 0.3%; Bitcoin tops $65,000 for the first time since June 17.

editions.headline: US and Iran Trade a Third Night of Strikes as CENTCOM Preps to Reimpose the Hormuz Blockade — Cooling CPI and a Bank Earnings Wall Collide on Wall Street
editions.teaser: US Central Command carries out a third straight night of strikes on Iran using one-way attack sea drones for the first time; June CPI cools sharply to 3.5% y/y; JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Bank of America and Goldman Sachs all beat earnings.

editions.headline: US and Iran Trade Fresh Strikes Overnight as Both Sides Dispute Whether the Strait of Hormuz Is Actually Open
editions.teaser: US Central Command carries out a fresh round of overnight strikes on Iran; Iran continues to insist the Strait of Hormuz is closed while CENTCOM maintains it remains open; Brent crude spikes to $79.29 before paring; KOSPI plunges 9%.

editions.headline: Iran Closes the Strait of Hormuz and Strikes Five Gulf Nations as the US Answers With a Third Round of Airstrikes
editions.teaser: Iran's IRGC disables the Cyprus-flagged container ship GFS Galaxy near Oman and declares the Strait of Hormuz closed "until further notice," prompting a third round of US airstrikes on roughly 140 Iranian targets; Tehran retaliates with missile and drone strikes on Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan and Oman.

editions.headline: Trump Says the Ceasefire Is "Over" but Iran Talks Will Continue — Wall Street Closes the Week Near Records on SK Hynix's Blockbuster Debut
editions.teaser: Trump insists the U.S.-Iran ceasefire remains "over" even as both sides agree to keep talking; SK Hynix's $26.5B Nasdaq debut headlines a records-adjacent Friday close; Bitcoin reclaims $64K.

editions.headline: Khamenei Laid to Rest in Mashhad as the Ceasefire He Died Over Stays Broken — Wall Street Looks Past It Toward SK Hynix
editions.teaser: Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is buried before dawn Friday at the Shrine of Imam Reza in Mashhad, closing a six-day funeral that drew over 15 million mourners, while the US-Iran ceasefire remains broken.

editions.headline: Trump Says U.S. "Already Won Militarily" as Iran Buries Khamenei in Mashhad — Markets Shrug Off a Second Night of Strikes
editions.teaser: Iran buries Ali Khamenei today at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad as the six-day state funeral concludes, even as the U.S. struck 80+ Iranian targets overnight for a second straight night.

editions.headline: Trump Declares Iran Ceasefire "Over" After U.S. Strikes 80+ Targets Overnight — Oil Surges 6%, Wall Street Braces for a Red Open
editions.teaser: President Trump declares the U.S.-Iran ceasefire "over" from the NATO summit in Ankara after Iran struck three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the U.S. retaliated with strikes on 80+ Iranian targets overnight.

editions.headline: Oil Tanker Struck Near Hormuz as Khamenei's Funeral Moves to Qom — Wall Street's Record Run Meets an Overnight Chip Wobble
